facts.value: The Mouseion lay within the royal palace quarter ("a part of the palaces"). Trans. Hamilton & Falconer (1854), Strabo 17.1.8.
facts.quote: The Museum is a part of the palaces.

facts.value: The Mouseion had a public walk (Greek peripatos). No dimensions given.
facts.quote: It has a public walk and a place furnished with seats, and a large hall

facts.value: A place furnished with seats (Greek exedra) adjoined the walk. No dimensions given.
facts.quote: a place furnished with seats

facts.value: A large hall where the resident scholars took their common meal. No dimensions given.
facts.quote: a large hall, in which the men of learning, who belong to the Museum, take their common meal

facts.value: All royal buildings, including the Mouseion, were connected with one another and with the harbour.
facts.quote: All the buildings are connected with one another and with the harbour

facts.value: The Sema, an enclosure with the tombs of the kings and Alexander, was also part of the palaces, adjoining the Mouseion in Strabo's list.
facts.quote: Sema, an enclosure, which contained the tombs of the kings and that of Alexander

facts.value: Daughter-library site: Serapeum with extensive columned halls and near-lifelike statues (Ammianus 22.16.12, Rolfe trans.). Rooms not itemised; no dimensions.
facts.quote: adorned with extensive columned halls, with almost breathing statues

facts.value: Ammianus says the Serapeum held "invaluable libraries". Translator footnote: Ammianus conflates the Bruchion and Serapeum libraries.
facts.quote: In this were invaluable libraries

facts.element: Serapeum: porticoes around open court with book rooms
facts.value: Bohn (1885), citing Aphthonius Progymn. 12, says Serapeum colonnades surrounded an open court with rooms behind them for books, matching Pergamon. Aphthonius original NOT fetched; second-hand.
facts.quote: Säulenhallen umgeben einen freien Platz, ... es ift alfo eine Anlage, welche mit der pergamenifchen übereinftimmt.
facts.note: Second-hand via Bohn; the OCR Greek quotation of Aphthonius is garbled, so wording of the rooms/books clause is not independently confirmed.

facts.value: 1944 excavation at the Column of Diocletian site yielded foundation deposits of a Temple of Serapis; Ptolemy III named as builder on the plaques. No library building found in this report.
facts.quote: Excavations in 1944 at the site of the column of Diocletian yielded the foundation deposits of a Temple of Serapis

facts.value: No excavated library building is claimed.
facts.note: Caution not proven: no fetched source states that no library building has been excavated. Only absence of any claim in sources above.

facts.value: Library rooms lay in the Athena sanctuary directly north of (behind) the north stoa, on rising rock.
facts.quote: Wir wenden uns jetzt den unmittelbar nördlich der Stoa gelegenen Baulichkeiten zu

facts.value: Two-storey stoa in front of the room block: Bohn refers to its Untergeschoss (lower storey) and a collapsed Obergeschoss. Inscription block found in the lower storey / forecourt debris. Column dimensions not extracted.
facts.quote: in dem frühzeitig zufammengeftürzten Obergefchoffe

facts.value: Bohn, following Conze: chambers fronted by a colonnade were typical in the Hellenistic-Roman period; parallels named: Serapeum library at Alexandria, Villa of the Papyri (Weber plan), Vitruvius VI.7.
facts.quote: Conze hat a. a. O. den Nachweis geführt, dafs die Verbindung von Gemächern mit einer Säulenhalle davor in helleniftifch-römifcher Zeit geradezu typifch war.

facts.value: Block of three rooms plus a larger fourth room to the east; Bohn counts four library rooms ("vier Bibliotheksräume").
facts.quote: Es bilden fich dergeftalt drei Gemächer, an welche fich örtlich noch ein viertes fchliefst

facts.value: Fourth room: depth 16.95 m, clear width 13.53 m (Bohn 1885). Wikipedia gives 13.6 x 15.2 m for the main room; Bohn figures preferred.
facts.quote: das aber durch gröfsere Tiefe, 16,95, ausgezeichnet ift; feine lichte Weite beträgt 13,53.

facts.value: Trachyte rear wall 1.05 m thick, running parallel to the stoa rear wall 14.40 m from its front edge; in places 8 courses (courses 0.30-0.44 m) survive.
facts.quote: läuft parallel mit der Rückwand, 14,40 von ihrer Vorderkante entfernt, eine Mauer aus Trachytfteinen.

facts.value: North wall: two slot holes 0.95 m above floor; a second row of 0.06 m square holes, 0.14 m deep, 1.05 m apart, also along the east wall. Bohn reads them as anchors for wooden shelving.
facts.quote: Löcher 0,060 im Quadrat, 0,14 in der Tiefe meffen und je 1,05 von einander entfernt

facts.value: Along the three standing walls, ~0.50 m from the wall, a foundation 1.05 m wide with dowel holes; upright slabs 0.465-0.470 m high and cover slabs 0.152 m high found nearby. Bohn: base for wooden book racks with a 0.50 m air gap.
facts.quote: Längs der drei noch flehenden Wände zieht fich in einem Abftand von etwa 0,50 ein Fundament von 1,05 Breite hin

facts.value: Central projection on the north wall: 2.74 m wide, projecting 1.05 m from the continuous foundation; Bohn takes it as the Athena statue stand.
facts.quote: in einer Breite von 2,74 ein befonderer Vorfprung um 1,05 heraus.

facts.value: Colossal Athena statue with figured base found in stoa debris directly in front of the room (about 2 m above lower-storey floor). Base width in OCR illegible; statue height not given by Bohn.
facts.quote: Koloffal- Statue der Athena

facts.value: Bohn conjectures only the wall plinth was clad in marble blocks, the upper wall plastered and painted (inferred from a parallel); trachyte backing wall. Heights not given.
facts.quote: dafs nur der Wandfockel (vgl. S. 42) mit Marmorquadern bekleidet, der obere Teil dagegen geputzt und bemalt gewefen fei.

facts.value: Bohn: walls abut rising ground (damp); the 0.50 m gap between wall and shelves would mitigate. Terracotta pipes (Thonrohrleitungen) belonged to the rooms.
facts.quote: Urfprünglich zu ihnen gehörige Thonrohrleitungen

facts.value: Ancient cistern cut deep into the rock near the south-east corner of the main room; rock-cut channel with collecting holes in front of the east part of the podium.
facts.quote: Nahe der Südoftecke befindet fleh eine anfeheinend aus dem Altertume herrührende, tief in den Felfen gearbeitete Cifterne.

facts.value: Layard & Rassam, spring 1852, in the South-West Palace (Sennacherib) at Kuyunjik: two small interconnected "chambers of records".
facts.quote: In one part of the building he found two small chambers, opening into each other, which he called the "chamber of records,"
facts.note: Budge (BM, 1920). Layard chapter below is the primary account.

facts.element: chambers of records: layout and wall decoration
facts.value: Entered via a doorway flanked by fish-god figures; two small chambers opening into each other, once panelled with bas-reliefs (mostly destroyed). No room dimensions in Layard.
facts.quote: led into two small chambers opening into each other, and once panelled with bas-reliefs

facts.value: Tablets lay on the floor to a depth of a foot or more (~0.3 m), mostly broken, probably by collapse of the upper building. No shelves described.
facts.quote: To the height of a foot or more from the floor they were entirely filled with them

facts.value: Largest tablets flat, about 9 x 6.5 inches (~0.23 x 0.17 m); smaller ones slightly convex, some about an inch (~0.025 m) long.
facts.quote: the largest tablets were flat, and measured about 9 inches by 6-1/2 inches

facts.element: North Palace: Chamber of the Lion Hunt
facts.value: Rassam, Dec 1853, North Palace (Ashurbanipal): lion-hunt relief chamber 50 x 15 ft (~15.2 x 4.6 m) in which heaps of tablets were found.
facts.quote: the chamber, which was 50 feet long and 15 feet wide, and illustrated a royal lion hunt

facts.value: Budge: no remains showed tablets were stored systematically there; they seem brought from elsewhere and thrown down. Original shelving/arrangement unknown.
facts.quote: There were no remains with them, or near them, that suggested they had been arranged systematically

facts.value: Budge states how tablets were arranged in the library is not known; groups were catalogued and some labelled.
facts.quote: How the tablets were arranged in the Library is not known

facts.value: Books were largely concentrated in one small room furnished with book cabinets (review of Sider, peer-reviewed venue). No dimensions fetched.
facts.quote: The books at the villa were largely concentrated in one small room, furnished with book cabinets

facts.value: Getty: some scrolls neatly stacked on shelves or in cases when found; early excavators mistook them for logs.
facts.quote: some of the book rolls were neatly stacked on shelves or in cases

facts.value: Wooden capsae on shelves around the walls and on a central double-sided shelf unit in the room.
facts.quote: some of them on ordinary wooden shelves and around the walls and some on the two sides of a set of shelves in the middle of the room

facts.value: Per Weber plan as described by Bohn 1885: library room lies behind a colonnade with a door opening into it.
facts.quote: hinter einer Säulenhalle liegt, mit einer Thür in diefe mündend.

facts.value: Karl Weber recorded findspots and architectural contexts (Getty).
facts.quote: Weber carefully recorded the objects’ findspots and architectural contexts.

facts.value: Xuanzang (Beal 1884): a high wall with one gate enclosed the sanghārāmas.
facts.quote: he built round these edifices a high wall with one gate.

facts.value: Xuanzang: monasteries added to the south, east, north-east, west and north of the first.
facts.quote: To the south of this he built another

facts.value: Xuanzang records a three-storeyed pavilion used for the assembly at Baladitya's monastery.
facts.quote: They led them up the three-storeyed pavilion.

facts.value: Site had a tank (Nalanda Naga) within an Amra (mango) grove.
facts.quote: there is a tank. The Naga of this tank is called Nalanda.

facts.value: Excavated vihara plan: rectangular, central quadrangular court, verandah, outer row of monk cells; shrine chamber facing entrance. Source is Wikipedia.
facts.quote: Their plan involves a rectangular form with a central quadrangular court which is surrounded by a verandah which, in turn, is bounded by an outer row of cells for the monks

facts.value: Later Tibetan tradition, not Xuanzang: library "Dharmaganja" of three large multi-storeyed buildings: Ratnasagara, Ratnodadhi, Ratnaranjaka. Not archaeologically identified.
facts.quote: a great library at Nalanda named Dharmaganja

facts.value: Tibetan tradition: Ratnodadhi nine storeys, held Prajnaparamita Sutra and Guhyasamaja.
facts.quote: Ratnodadhi was nine storeys high and housed the most sacred manuscripts

facts.value: Library hall on the Danube side of Buda Castle, near the royal chapel and throne hall, per Naldo Naldi's account (via corvina.hu).
facts.quote: the library hall, located on the Danube side of the Buda Castle, near the royal chapel and the throne hall

facts.value: Bookcases with inlaid decoration; open shelves protected from dust by heavy red curtains (Naldi).
facts.quote: had been furnished with bookcases with inlaid decoration. The open shelves had been protected against dust with heavy red curtains

facts.value: Double windows fitted with stained glass (Naldi).
facts.quote: the double windows had been fitted with stained glass

facts.value: Two high vaulted rooms (Greek / Latin) reported by secondary sources.
facts.note: Not fetched: tertullian.org (Csapodi) timed out; UNESCO nomination returned no text. Search snippets only, so unproven.
